These are fresh public official responses acquired for VS-04. `manifest.json` records the requested and final URLs, response status, capture time, original response hash, saved hash, and credential-redaction count. Text responses enter through `writeCapturedFixture`; binary files retain their exact bytes. HTTP 200 alone is not evidence of a polling list: several saved county URLs returned ordinary error pages or unrelated content, and none became configured location sources.

`nc-november-polling.csv.bin` preserves the original UTF-16 CSV response, including its NUL bytes and one decoded NUL placeholder. The binary extension keeps those publisher bytes outside source-text searches; decoding and placeholder removal happen only in the reader. Renaming this capture leaves its saved SHA-256 unchanged.

`config-fragment.json` contains the successful state-file and county-file mappings. `parsed-sources.json` records the first five-state extraction pass. `source-read-results.json` records saved-response reader runs using the real captured robots responses. The production-copy worker owns publication/readback proof; these local extraction results do not claim production publication.

Working routes:

| State | Source and coverage |
| --- | --- |
| AL | Mobile County Probate Court's current 2026 polling PDF: 78 sites. The state lookup has voter identity and address-search forms; no voter lookup was submitted. Other counties remain open. |
| FL | State Division of Elections' 2026 General ZIP contains all 67 county PDFs. Repeated labeled PDF blocks provide early-voting locations and explicit ballot-intake flags. There are 466 printed early-location blocks; same-source services combine into 463 physical sites. Separate additional-intake sections and full daily schedules remain open. |
| GA | Cobb County's public September 2026 precinct PDF: all 148 precinct rows and 132 facilities. The SOS county directory returned 403; the county's own .gov files worked. Other counties remain open. |
| KY | State Board of Elections' current workbook has separate election-day, excused in-person, no-excuse in-person, and drop-box sheets: 1,690 combined facilities across 120 counties. All four mappings combine before replacing this source's prior publication. The excused sheet omits Larue County and lists two Bell County facilities. |
| MS | DeSoto County's currently linked precinct map includes 46 facilities. The map is revised March 7, 2025; November 2026 applicability and other counties remain open. |
| NC | The state polling-data page now links the November 3, 2026 CSV, replacing the earlier March fallback: 2,626 precinct rows and 2,610 facilities across all 100 counties. The statewide early-voting TSV holds 6,239 dated rows and 367 facilities across all 100 counties. Extracting the published city from both formats merges shared facilities into 2,806 combined sites. A NUL placeholder in one city cell is removed only from decoded text; saved response bytes remain intact. |
| SC | The state's public CSV export has 2,358 precinct rows and 1,956 facilities in all 46 counties. The publisher explicitly excludes temporary election-specific polling changes; November-specific assignments remain open. |
| TN | Davidson County's current November 3 early-voting page lists 15 facilities. State identity lookup forms were recorded without submission; county public lists were used instead. Other counties and daily schedule extraction remain open. |
| VA | The state's November General workbook has 2,817 rows and 2,651 facilities across 133 printed county-equivalent labels. Its SpreadsheetML uses element namespaces and omits cell-coordinate attributes; both are valid spreadsheet formats now supported by the common reader. |
| WV | The state's early-voting page has 99 locations across all 55 counties. Each facility's adjacent date row is captured, preserving shorter satellite periods instead of assigning every facility the statewide dates. |

Reusable methods: follow the chief office's actual download link rather than guessing file names; accept UTF-16 tab-separated CSV with its original bytes held; read each named workbook sheet as an independent service; retain the public ZIP as the cited document while extracting its exact named PDF member; identify repeated PDF blocks by printed headings rather than fixed page coordinates; derive PDF titles from visual heading order so schedule dates cannot become a false older-election title; use official county polling files when voter identity forms are the available state lookup; retain publisher warnings and earlier dates as acquisition work.
